title: Boneless Chicken Thighs with Sweet Potato & Fresh Spinach
displayTitle: Boneless Chicken Thighs with Sweet Potato & Fresh Spinach
seoTitle: Boneless Chicken Thighs with Sweet Potato & Fresh Spinach | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Seared thighs with roasted sweet potato and garlicky spinach
subtitle: Seared thighs with roasted sweet potato and garlicky spinach
description: Boneless chicken thighs sear golden in a hot skillet while sweet potato wedges roast until caramelized. Fresh spinach hits garlic oil at the line for a complete performance plate.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Boneless Chicken Thighs with Sweet Potato & Fresh Spinach in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Season and prep thighs
steps.instruction: Trim excess fat from thighs and pat completely dry. Season both sides with salt, pepper, and half the paprika so the sear builds a spiced crust.

steps.title: Roast sweet potato wedges
steps.instruction: Toss wedges with 2 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp salt, and paprika. Spread on two half-sheets in a single layer. Roast at 425°F 28–32 minutes until edges caramelize and centers pierce easily.

steps.title: Sear chicken thighs
steps.instruction: Heat remaining oil in skillets over medium-high. Season thighs with salt and pepper. Sear 5–6 minutes per side until deep golden with crisp edges and internal temp reaches 165°F. Rest 5 minutes, then slice.

steps.title: Sauté spinach
steps.instruction: In the same pan over medium, cook garlic 30 seconds until fragrant. Add spinach in batches, tossing until just wilted and bright green. Finish with a pinch of salt and lemon juice.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Boneless Chicken Thighs with Sweet Potato & Fresh Spinach onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Plate for service
steps.instruction: Portion two sliced thighs per plate with a mound of sweet potato wedges and sautéed spinach on the side. Protein should dominate the plate; vegetables and carbs stay distinct, not mixed into sauce.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Boneless Chicken Thighs with Sweet Potato & Fresh Spinach — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: Swap half the paprika for cumin if crews want a warmer spice profile.
Hold roasted wedges in a 200°F oven while batch-searing thighs on busy nights.
Offer hot sauce at the line—keeps the plate lean without extra fat.
tonightSpread: Brown rice for crews wanting extra carbs.
leftovers: Slice thighs over spinach for next-day power bowls.
Re-crisp sweet potato wedges in a hot oven 8 minutes.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Clean protein-forward plate without stew vibes. Thighs stay juicy, sweet potato fuels the shift, spinach adds volume without feeling like diet food.
mealPrepNotes: Cut sweet potato wedges uniform for even roasting. Pat thighs completely dry before searing. Station: Roast sweet potatoes first—they hold hot while thighs sear to order. Station: Sear thighs in batches; crowded pans steam instead of brown. Station: Wilt spinach off heat so it stays bright green at service.
